name: TAIWAN

flag.title: Republic of China
flag.note: Red field, blue canton, white sun of 12 rays

lead: Taiwan is a lush, mountainous island off China's coast. Portuguese sailors named it "Formosa" — beautiful island — in 1542, and it still fits. Half is steep forested peaks; the rest is flat farmland and buzzing cities. Taiwan makes most of the world's most advanced chips and invented bubble tea, now loved everywhere.
geo: Taiwan sits on the Pacific Ring of Fire — the island gets about 1,000 small earthquakes a year. The Central Mountain Range runs like a spine down the middle, with nearly 200 peaks topping 3,000 m.
The east coast drops dramatically into the Pacific. Taroko Gorge cuts a stunning marble canyon through the mountains, its turquoise river carving walls 1,000 m high.
animals: Taiwan's forests hide the Formosan black bear — a shy giant with a V-shaped yellow chest patch locals call the "moon bear". Up in the misty peaks, the Mikado pheasant glows iridescent blue-purple.
Every winter, millions of purple crow butterflies migrate to Maolin valley to shelter from the cold — a living purple blizzard stretching as far as you can see.
culture: Night markets are Taiwan's living rooms — open-air bazaars where you eat stinky tofu, oyster omelettes, and shaved ice topped with fresh mango. Bubble tea — chewy tapioca pearls in sweet milk tea — was invented in Taichung in the 1980s.

Lantern Festival each February sees thousands of sky lanterns released over Pingxi, wishes written in ink floating upward. Over 15,000 temples dot the island — more per square kilometre than almost anywhere on Earth.
history: Aboriginal Austronesian peoples settled Taiwan at least 6,000 years ago. Dutch traders arrived in 1624, then Chinese settlers poured in. Japan controlled the island 1895–1945, building railways and schools.

After World War II, Taiwan's Nationalist government fled mainland China in 1949. The island transformed from a farming economy into a technology powerhouse — today it makes roughly 90% of the world's most advanced microchips.
wows: Taiwan's TSMC produces roughly 90% of the world's most advanced chips — the brains inside every smartphone.
Bubble tea was invented in Taichung, Taiwan, in the 1980s and is now a global industry.
Taipei's metro has a punctuality rate above 99.7% — among the most reliable in the world.
Taiwan has one convenience store for every 1,700 people — more per person than almost any country.
Yushan (Jade Mountain) is nearly 180 m taller than Japan's famous Mount Fuji.
Taroko Gorge is carved almost entirely from marble — one of Earth's largest marble canyons.
Taiwan's Lantern Festival releases so many sky lanterns the sky turns orange above the hills.

myths.myth: Taiwan is just part of China
myths.fact: Taiwan has had its own elected government, military, currency, and passport since 1949 — a self-governing democracy, though its international status is disputed.
The smell is famously pungent, but fans say the taste is mild — crispy outside, soft inside, and surprisingly addictive once you brave the first bite.
